comparisons.peer_topic: Inventory write-down impact on gross margin
comparisons.peer_summary: If assumptions regarding future demand or market conditions become less favorable, additional inventory write-downs may be required, negatively impacting gross margin; conversely, selling previously written-down inventory above its written-down value may result in a net benefit to gross margin.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address specific operational risks that could negatively impact financial performance, but they differ in the nature of the risk driver. NVDA cites geopolitical factors (export controls) limiting supply chain flexibility, whereas AMD cites market factors (demand assumptions) affecting inventory valuation. NVDA's risk is external and regulatory, while AMD's risk is internal and market-driven.

sentences.text: While we work to enhance the resiliency and redundancy of our supply chain, which is currently concentrated in the Asia-Pacific region, new and existing export controls or changes to existing export controls could limit alternative manufacturing locations and negatively impact our business.

If in any period we anticipate a change in assumptions such as future demand or market conditions to be less favorable than our previous estimates, additional inventory write-downs may be required and would be reflected in cost of sales, resulting in a negative impact to our gross margin in that period.
